content.title: About
content.content: The beef and cheese burrito is a Mexican dish consisting of a large flour or corn tortilla wrapped around a filling of sautéed beef, melted cheese, rice, beans, and spices. Served hot, it is often accompanied by salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico in the early 20th century as a portable meal for workers.
Traditional Mexican burritos are modest in size, while U.S. versions are frequently much larger.
The combination of beef and cheese provides a rich umami flavor prized by meat lovers.
Beef‑cheese burritos often include chipotle or ground cumin to boost aroma.
Because of their high protein content, burritos are popular among athletes as a hearty post‑workout meal.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef and cheese are excellent sources of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron source
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium needed for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbs
items.content: Rice and beans provide quick‑release carbohydrates, useful for fueling physical activity.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef offers vitamin B12, while beans provide folate, both important for nervous system health and blood formation.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Cheese and beef can be high in saturated fats, so individuals with cardiovascular concerns should limit portion size.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared sauces and cheese often contain added salt, which may raise blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with milk protein allergy or lactose intolerance should choose dairy‑free cheese alternatives.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A burrito is calorie‑rich; overconsumption can contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are conveniently eaten by hand, often cut in half. Serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or fresh cilantro. For a lighter version, use a whole‑grain tortilla and reduce the amount of cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze it wrapped in plastic; reheat in the microwave or on a skillet before serving.
